drivers.variant_notes: The only PinMAME driver for game 510; its five ROM members match the pinned s7games.c SHA-1 values and the parts supplement's ROM summary (Sound ROM 4). Source comments name a tournament ROM mod and a 2x/3x playfield multiplier mod; neither is a driver and neither is covered here.

physical.notes: Cabinet sheet 7SW75 ADVANCE on CPU connector 1J4-3 (GRN, 7P1-5). Steps the diagnostic tests and adjustments together with Auto-Up/Manual-Down; the harness pressed it to walk Test 02 and Test 03.

Cabinet sheet 7SW74, positions AUTO-UP and MANUAL-DOWN, on CPU connector 1J4-4 (BLU, 7P1-6). PinMAME's Auto/Manual input is a toggle that reads 1 for Auto-Up; a two-position switch has no rest state, and normally_closed follows that public convention.

The CPU board's DIAGNOSTIC pushbutton (booklet CPU Board Self-Test; the assembly view draws it beside IC24, and its TP2 inset shows the NMI line low while it is depressed). s7.c asserts the CPU's NMI while this input is 1.

Sound board SW1, MOMENTARY SWITCH SPDT (bill of material item 46); pressing it starts the booklet's Sound Board Self-Test, a sequence of sounds that repeats until the game is turned off and on again. s7.c passes the input to the S67S sound board, which asserts the sound CPU's NMI while it is 1. Which throw of the SPDT part the board uses was not read; the press-to-activate contact is recorded.

s7.c's s7_dips_r returns the F and D DIP nibbles only while this input is held. No Master Command Enter control appears in the cabinet wiring or the CPU board assembly view; the CPU bill of material counts two momentary switches against a note that was not read, and only the DIAGNOSTIC pushbutton is drawn. The booklet's adjustment procedures use Advance and Auto-Up/Manual-Down only. Optional emulator input; nothing in play needs it.

mechanisms.behavior: Three balls rest on the ball ramp positions 13, 14 and 15 (15 at the thrower end) or, at most one, in the shooter lane on 16; a game starts only then. Start fires the ball ramp thrower 12, which serves the ball at 15 into the shooter lane, and the remaining balls roll down the ramp. The player plunges by hand. A drained ball rests on outhole switch 12 and ball release 11 kicks it onto the ball ramp. The gameplay run observes 12 on Start and on each lock, and 11 on an outhole closure; the host moved every ball, so ramp travel times are not measured.
mechanisms.label: Outhole, ball ramp and thrower

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets (the parts supplement's 3-bank, first used in Barracora). Each target switch is closed while its target is down. Bank release 9 drops the whole bank; reset coils 1, 2 and 3 raise one target each. Start fires 9 and then 1-3 (with 10 and 4-8). Making B, A, RR in sequence spots BARRACORA lamps; the gameplay run raises a target knocked down out of sequence at once (3 alone for RR) and, on completing the bank in sequence, raises 3, 2, 1 one at a time with no bank release. Completing it advances the bonus multiplier and lights the lower eject hole lock arrow. Drop targets are remembered per player.
mechanisms.label: B-A-RR 3-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Five drop targets, 44 at the top to 48 at the bottom. Bank release 10 drops the bank; reset coils 4-8 raise one target each. Completing the bank in sequence raises 8, 7, 6, 5, 4 one at a time in the gameplay run, advances the bonus multiplier and lights the upper eject hole lock arrow; completing both banks advances the super bonus multiplier.
mechanisms.label: A-C-O-R-A 5-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Kick-out hole at the top left. Ball-presence switch 10 is closed while a ball rests in it; kicker 13 ejects it. With its lock arrow lit, a ball entering locks: the gameplay run serves a new ball with thrower 12 0.18 s after 10 closes. 5.14 s after the plunge that follows the second lock, the gate 17 energizes and 13 kicks the locked ball out. With lamps 1-6 complete it also collects the bonus.
mechanisms.label: Upper eject hole

mechanisms.behavior: Ball Gate Lock Assembly (coil, armature and return spring) at the mouth of the upper eject hole. The gameplay run energizes 17 5.13 s after the shooter switch 16 opens and keeps it on in play, drops it 0.03 s after the thrower serves the next ball for an upper-hole lock, and energizes it again just before 13 releases the locked ball. The VR Room script opens the table's gate while 17 is on and closes it when 17 drops. The retained pages do not draw the gate's swing, so whether energized means open on the machine is the script's reading, not a drawn fact.
mechanisms.label: Upper eject hole gate

mechanisms.behavior: Kick-out hole on the left below the upper hole. Ball-presence switch 11 is closed while a ball rests in it; kicker 14 ejects it. With its lock arrow lit, a ball entering starts 2-ball Multi-Ball, or 3-ball when a ball is already locked above: the gameplay run serves a new ball with 12 3.09 s after 11 closes, and kicks 14 when the upper hole's switch 10 opens during the 3-ball release. A ball locked first here gives only 2-ball play.
mechanisms.label: Lower eject hole

mechanisms.behavior: Three top rollover lanes 17, 18 and 19 light lamps 1, 2 and 3, or 4, 5 and 6 beneath an already lit one. The flipper buttons rotate the lit lamps (Lane Change): PinMAME copies the right button into 35 and the left into 34. Lamps 1-3 advance the lower eject hole values, lamps 4-6 the upper right bull's-eye values, and all six light the upper eject hole bonus collect. The gameplay run lit lamp 17 from lane 17 and the right button moved it to 18.
mechanisms.label: Top lanes and Lane Change

mechanisms.behavior: Left Jet Bumper: scoring matrix switch 20 and a separate direct-drive special switch on the same assembly fire special solenoid 18 through the special driver while game-on 25 enables it. PinMAME derives slot 18 from 20; the gameplay run fires 18 within 20 ms of a closure. Power and stroke are table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Left Jet Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Left Kicker: scoring matrix switch 29 and a separate direct-drive special switch on the same assembly fire special solenoid 21 through the special driver while game-on 25 enables it. mechanisms.behavior: One right flipper with a dual-wound SFL-19-400/30-750-DC coil and its own flipper contact, switched by the cabinet button through relay Z1 while game-on 25 holds it. A consumer drives button 82; PinMAME fabricates 45/46 together and copies the button into lane-change switch 35. Travel, end-of-stroke behavior and tuning belong to the table.
